Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs Justice P Sree Sudha
 Oral Judgment
1.
This appeal is preferred by the claimants against the Judgment and award dated 01.12.2021 in MVC No.5/2021 by the MACT and Addl.
Senior Civil Judge, Bidar, (for short 'the tribunal') seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the tribunal.
2. One Mansoth Mohan S/o. M.Surya, met with accident on 08.1.2020 and succumbed to the injuries.
Claimant No.1 is the mother and claimant No.2 is the father of the deceased Mansoth Mohan.
They filed claim petition NC: 2025:KHC-K:6616 HC-KAR before the tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.60,00,000/-.

The tribunal after considering the entire evidence on record,
awarded a sum of Rs.19,24,400/- along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Aggrieved by the said Judgment and award, the claimant preferred the present appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation.
3. It is mainly contended that, the deceased was getting salary of Rs.15,000/- per month and also doing motor vehicle winding works and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

But the tribunal has Mainsath Shanthi And Anr vs Nenavath Sakku And Anr on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83113257/
2 considered only Rs.12,000/- per month.

entities.text: Mainsath Shanthi And Anr vs Nenavath Sakku And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, he requests for enhancement of the compensation awarded by the tribunal.
4. Though the appellants stated that the deceased was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, they have not produced any income proof.
Hence, as he met with an accident in the year 2020, as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, his notional income is to be taken as Rs.13,750/- per month.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6616 HC-KAR 5.

As per the dictum of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi1, considering the age of the deceased, 40% of the income has to be added towards future prospects, which is rightly considered by the Tribunal.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The multiplier of 18 and the deductions towards personal expenses of the deceased at 50% considered by the Tribunal are also just and proper.
6. Therefore, the loss of dependency comes to 13,750 + 40% - 50% x 12 x 18 = Rs.20,07,900).

7. Further, as per the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the dictum of Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & others2, and United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others3, the appellants being the parents of the deceased (2017) 16 SCC 680 (2018) 18 SCC 130 (2020) 9 SCC 644 NC:
2025:KHC-K:6616 HC-KAR are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each towards loss of filial consortium.
8.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: They are also entitled for an amount of Rs.30,000/- under the conventional heads i.e., loss of estate and funeral expenses as per the citation in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
9. Hence, the compensation is reassessed as under:
Loss of dependency Rs.20,79,000/-
Loss of consortium Rs.88,000/-
Conventional heads Rs.30,000/-
Total Rs.21,97,000/-
Less awarded by the Tribunal: Rs.19,24,400/-
Enhanced compensation Rs.2,72,600/-
The Insurance Company has already deposited the amount awarded by the Tribunal.

Thus, the appellants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.2,72,600/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

However, as per order dated 30.10.2023, they are not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 290 days in filing the appeal.
(iii) Respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within one month from the date of this judgment.
